title: Local caches cap the shard's load at servers ÷ TTL, whatever the audience size
caption: Each app server refreshes its own copy at most once per TTL, so millions of readers become a few hundred reads/s at the shard.

steps.text: A flash sale: a million shoppers keep refreshing one product page, about 800 000 reads/s for one key.
They spread over 200 app servers, ~4 000 reads/s each, all answered from an in-process copy in microseconds.
Each server refreshes its copy at most once per 2 s TTL: 200 / 2 = 100 reads/s reach the shard. The price is up to 2 s of staleness.

scenarios.name: Alternative: key splitting
scenarios.summary: Store N copies of the hot key on N shards and read a random one: no per-server staleness, but every write must update all N, and each read still costs a network hop.
scenarios.caption: Splitting spreads one key's reads over N shards; local caching removes most of them.

steps.text: Each read picks r = random(0..3) and GETs product:77#r. The suffix lands each copy on a different shard.
Each shard serves a quarter of the reads. 800 000/s needs N ≈ 10 copies for ~100k per shard.
A price change must SET every copy. Until the last one lands, readers can see two different prices.

scenarios.name: Risk: stale price
scenarios.summary: Local copies serve the old value until their TTL runs out, independently on each server. Keep TTLs short and never trust a local copy for money.

steps.text: The price drops from 50 to 40 and the shard is updated.
Each app server still holds its own copy for up to 2 s, so shoppers on different servers see different prices.
Mitigation: a short TTL, a pub/sub message that evicts the local copies early, and checkout that reads the authoritative value.

scenarios.name: Shard goes down
scenarios.summary: With serve-stale-on-error, local copies keep the page up while the shard is gone: readers get a slightly old value instead of an error.

steps.text: Refreshes fail, but each server keeps its last copy instead of deleting it on expiry.
Shoppers keep getting pages, older than 2 s but correct enough, while the replica is promoted.
